requirement:
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
rationale: I found no gap. Every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.details` has code that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome. **Detail subchapter for each record, under the index chapter** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate_in]`, reached from `fn[populate]`, builds one `Chapter` for every `Record`. - It appends those chapters to the index chapter's `sub_items`. The summary table links to each one, and the summary table lists every record. - `fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` asserts `index.sub_items.len() == 4`. It also checks that the index links to each detail chapter. **Binary, test name, attempt, outcome and originating run** - `fn[detail]` writes "Binary / Test / Attempt / Outcome", then "Run: id (run outcome)", then the capture time. - The test above asserts `Binary: binary`, `Test: one`, `Attempt`, `Outcome`, `Captured at Unix ns` and `Run: {first_run}`. **Instrumented first-party lines, counts, executed vs unexecuted, and the source captured for that run** - `fn[detail]` emits the per-process lines as JSON, with counts as strings so full u64 values survive. - It also emits the `assets/coverage-viewer.js` renderer, and `fn[source_page]` writes a per-run captured-source chapter. - The viewer prints "N executed" or "0 unexecuted" beside each line's captured source text. It reports a missing source as unavailable. - The JS test `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs` checks all of this: - It checks the counter `18446744073709551615 executed` and `0 unexecuted`. - It checks that the captured source text is used and that messages from unrelated windows or other runs are ignored. - It checks that file rendering is lazy. - The Rust test `fn[rendered_detail_scripts_remain_literal_across_blank_lines]` checks that the rendered Markdown keeps the script literal and the counts intact. - `fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` checks that the saved source and counts survive source edits. **Link back to the index** - `fn[detail]` and `fn[source_page]` both write `[Back to coverage index]`. The Rust test asserts `[Back to coverage index](../coverage.html)`. **Child-process coverage stays distinguishable** - `fn[detail]` labels each process `"Test"` when `process.pid == attempt.pid` and `"Child"` otherwise. - The viewer renders each as a separate heading, `${kind} process ${pid}`, with its own counters. - The Rust test asserts both `"kind":"Test"` and `"kind":"Child"`, plus the child's counts `"1":"0","2":"7"`. The JS test asserts `Child process 2`. **Other checks** - The extra behaviour in the code is the per-process diagnostics, the "no process report" notice and the noscript note. It falls within what the requirement describes and the related index requirements that the same code marks with {impl}. - No `{fixme}` references are involved.

text: :::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
